claim: Cerebellar granule neurons (CGNs) comprise more than 99% of all neurons in the cerebellum.
source: We use CGNs to model neurodevelopment because they comprise more than 99% of all neurons (Consalez et al., 2021) and 85% of cells (Altman and Bayer, 1997) in the cerebellum
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Consalez et al., 2021

claim: CGNs comprise 85% of cells in the cerebellum.
source: We use CGNs to model neurodevelopment because they comprise more than 99% of all neurons (Consalez et al., 2021) and 85% of cells (Altman and Bayer, 1997) in the cerebellum
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Altman and Bayer, 1997

claim: Global H3K27me3 levels significantly increase from P7 to P14 in mouse cerebellum.
source: Western blot of acid-extracted histones showed a significant global increase in total H3K27me3 levels from P7 to P14 that was maintained at P60 (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B with statistical significance indicated

claim: Global H3K27me3 levels are maintained from P14 to P60 in mouse cerebellum.
source: Western blot of acid-extracted histones showed a significant global increase in total H3K27me3 levels from P7 to P14 that was maintained at P60 (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B

claim: Total H3K27ac levels decrease from P7 to P14 in mouse cerebellum.
source: whereas total H3K27ac fell in a similar temporal pattern (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: The global increase in H3K27me3 is consistent with PRC2-dependent restriction of cell potential upon terminal differentiation.
source: These data are consistent with the PRC2-dependent restriction of cell potential upon terminal differentiation (van Mierlo et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the data and citation to van Mierlo et al., 2019

claim: 660 H3K27me3 peaks are gained between P7 and P14 in mouse cerebellum.
source: MA plots showing H3K27me3 peaks gained (Up) and lost (Down) throughout cerebellar maturation in vivo (n=3 biological replicates, differential enrichment calculated using DESeq2 package. Up and Down are loci with FDR <0.05 and |L2FC|>2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: 602 H3K27me3 peaks are lost between P7 and P14 in mouse cerebellum.
source: MA plots showing H3K27me3 peaks gained (Up) and lost (Down) throughout cerebellar maturation in vivo (n=3 biological replicates, differential enrichment calculated using DESeq2 package. Up and Down are loci with FDR <0.05 and |L2FC|>2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: Bidirectional changes in H3K27me3 distributions occur during postmitotic stages of neuronal maturation.
source: This was true even when comparing P14 with P60 (Figure 1C), demonstrating that bidirectional changes in H3K27me3 distributions occur during postmitotic stages of neuronal maturation, well after the period of terminal cell fate commitment has ended
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data comparing P14 and P60 shown in Figure 1C

claim: Promoters are overrepresented among developmentally demethylated H3K27me3 peaks.
source: We stratified differential H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks by their genomic location with respect to proximal gene promoters, gene bodies, or intergenic regions (Figure 1D), and found a consistent overrepresentation of proximal gene promoters among developmentally demethylated peaks for all three comparisons.
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic annotation analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: H3K27me3 peaks differentially gained during development do not differ from the global distribution of H3K27me3.
source: By contrast, H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks differentially gained between all three comparisons did not differ from the global distribution of H3K27me3, which was distributed across gene-body and distal intergenic regions as well as proximal promoters.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of differential peaks to global H3K27me3 distribution

claim: The percentage of H3K27me3-positive promoters decreases approximately twofold from P7 to P60.
source: The percentage of total H3K27me3-positive promoters gradually decreased by ~ twofold from P7 to P60
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K27me3 peak distribution over time

claim: The percentage of H3K27me3-positive distal intergenic regions increases from P7 to P60.
source: while that of H3K27me3-positive distal intergenic regions increased
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K27me3 peak distribution over time

claim: The percentage of H3K27me3-positive gene bodies remains approximately the same from P7 to P60.
source: and that of gene bodies stayed about the same over time
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K27me3 peak distribution over time

claim: H3K27me3 patterns are locally regulated in postmitotic neurons.
source: These data demonstrate that in CGNs H3K27me3 patterns are locally regulated in postmitotic neurons
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed bidirectional changes in H3K27me3 at specific genomic locations

claim: H3K27me3 has a function in developing neurons that extends beyond the restriction of cell fate commitment.
source: suggesting a function for H3K27me3-dependent gene regulation in developing neurons that extends beyond the restriction of cell fate commitment.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that H3K27me3 continues to change after cell fate commitment

claim: 3618 differential H3K27me3 peaks were identified across P7, P14, and P60 using a cutoff of |Log2FC|>2, p-adj <0.05.
source: We identified 3618 differential H3K27me3 peaks across all time points using a strict cut-off of |Log2FC|>2, p-adj <0.05.
evidence: The claim is supported by differential peak analysis using DESeq2

claim: 1805 differential H3K27me3 peaks are located at promoters.
source: We first filtered these for promoters because these regions can be directly mapped to their target gene for transcriptional regulation and obtained 1805 peaks.
evidence: The claim is supported by filtering differential peaks for promoter regions

claim: Grin2c loses H3K27me3 at its promoter from P7 to P60.
source: Examples of genes with promoter-associated peaks lost or gained from P7 to P60, respectively, were the genes encoding the mature NMDA-type glutamate receptor Grin2c which is strongly expressed in mature CGNs (Wijayatunge et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq tracks shown in Figure 1F and citation

claim: Mycn gains H3K27me3 at its promoter from P7 to P60.
source: and the cell-proliferation factor Mycn, which is expressed only in GNPs (Ma et al., 2015; Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq tracks shown in Figure 1F and citation

claim: Changes in promoter H3K27me3 levels inversely correlate with changes in gene expression over development.
source: This is consistent with the hypothesis that changes in the levels of promoter H3K27me3 inversely correlate with changes in gene expression over development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the examples of Grin2c and Mycn

claim: Hierarchical clustering of differential H3K27me3 promoter peaks identified three major clusters.
source: To determine if the correlation of H3K27me3 demethylation with transcriptional maturation holds broadly, we first performed hierarchical clustering on the 1805 differential H3K27me3 promoter peaks and identified three major clusters with differing direction and timing of change (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 2A

claim: The 'H3K27me3 Up' cluster contains peaks that gain methylation as early as P14 and maintain methylation during CGN maturation.
source: The first cluster, which we termed 'H3K27me3 Up,' contained peaks that gained methylation as early as P14 and maintained methylation during CGN maturation.
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis

claim: The 'H3K27me3 Down (Fast)' cluster contains peaks that change between P7 and P14.
source: The next two clusters included demethylated peaks, that we termed 'H3K27me3 Down (Fast)' and 'H3K27me3 Down (Slow)', respectively, depending on whether they changed between P7 and P14 or between P14 and P60.
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis

claim: The 'H3K27me3 Down (Slow)' cluster contains peaks that change between P14 and P60.
source: The next two clusters included demethylated peaks, that we termed 'H3K27me3 Down (Fast)' and 'H3K27me3 Down (Slow)', respectively, depending on whether they changed between P7 and P14 or between P14 and P60.
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis

claim: Most promoters with differential H3K27me3 have H3K4me3 peaks at both P6 and P22.
source: Regardless of their H3K27me3 dynamics, most of these promoters had peaks of H3K4me3 at both P6 and P22 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K4me3 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B

claim: Promoters that gain H3K27me3 show a significant decrease in H3K4me3 levels over time.
source: However, these data also show that, compared with the set of promoters that have unchanged H3K27me3 over development, there was a significant decrease in H3K4me3 levels over time at promoters that gain H3K27me3
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K4me3 levels at differential H3K27me3 promoters

claim: Promoters that lose H3K27me3 show a significant increase in H3K4me3 levels over time.
source: whereas there is a significant increase in H3K4me3 at promoters that lose H3K27me3 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K4me3 levels at differential H3K27me3 promoters shown in Figure 2B

claim: Changes in H3K27me3 inversely correlate with H3K27ac enrichment at the same promoters.
source: Further consistent with the hypothesis that turnover of promoter H3K27me3 permits promoter activation, we saw an inverse correlation between changes in H3K27me3 and enrichment of the active chromatin marker H3K27ac as well as chromatin accessibility (Frank et al., 2015) at the same promoters (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K27ac ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Changes in H3K27me3 inversely correlate with chromatin accessibility at the same promoters.
source: Further consistent with the hypothesis that turnover of promoter H3K27me3 permits promoter activation, we saw an inverse correlation between changes in H3K27me3 and enrichment of the active chromatin marker H3K27ac as well as chromatin accessibility (Frank et al., 2015) at the same promoters (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of DNase-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation

claim: The 'H3K27me3 Up' cluster is enriched for genes associated with cell proliferation and development.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis showed the H3K27me3 Up category to be enriched for genes associated with progenitor functional terms related to cell proliferation and development
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis

claim: The 'H3K27me3 Down (Fast)' and 'H3K27me3 Down (Slow)' clusters are enriched for neuronal GO terms.
source: whereas the H3K27me3 Down (Fast) and Down (Slow) clusters were both enriched for neuronal GO terms (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 2C

claim: 'H3K27me3 Up' peaks at gene promoters are significantly associated with decreased gene expression over developmental time.
source: We found that 'H3K27me3 Up' peaks at gene promoters were significantly associated with a decrease in expression of the associated gene over the same period of developmental time
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between H3K27me3 ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: 'H3K27me3 Down' peaks at gene promoters are significantly associated with increased gene expression over developmental time.
source: and 'H3K27me3 Down' peaks were associated with an increase in gene expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between H3K27me3 ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: 'H3K27me3 Down (Fast)' peaks are associated with greater magnitude of gene induction than 'Slow' peaks between P7 and P14.
source: Among the H3K27me3 Down peaks, 'Fast' peaks were associated with a significantly greater magnitude of gene induction than 'Slow' peaks between P7 and P14
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of gene expression changes between clusters

claim: 'H3K27me3 Down (Slow)' peaks are associated with greater magnitude of gene induction than 'Fast' peaks between P14 and P60.
source: but 'Slow' peaks were associated with a significantly greater magnitude of gene induction than 'Fast' peaks between P14 and P60.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of gene expression changes between clusters

claim: There is no significant difference in magnitude of gene expression change between 'Fast' and 'Slow' peaks from P7 to P60.
source: There was no significant difference between 'Fast' and 'Slow' peaks from P7 to P60 indicating that it is the timing not the magnitude of differential developmental gene expression that defines the two clusters.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of gene expression changes between clusters

claim: H3K27me3 dynamics at gene promoters are associated with the timing of gene expression changes in postmitotic neurons.
source: These data show that the H3K27me3 dynamics at gene promoters are associated with differential H3K4me3 enrichment, and the timing of gene expression changes in postmitotic neurons, which allows for multiple postmitotic waves of gene expression (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis of H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E

claim: 1813 differential non-promoter H3K27me3 peaks were identified.
source: To determine whether the non-promoter H3K27me3 peaks we identified in developing cerebellum might function to regulate enhancers, we assessed our differential H3K27me3 sites for histone markers that are characteristic of enhancers.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the total differential peaks (3618) minus promoter peaks (1805)

claim: 207 differential non-promoter H3K27me3 peaks overlap with H3K4me1 peaks, representing putative co-labeled enhancers.
source: Thus, we first computed the overlap of the 1813 differential non-promoter H3K27me3 peaks with H3K4me1 peaks derived from P9 cerebellum (Ramirez et al., 2022) and found 207 putative co-labeled enhancers (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis with H3K4me1 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A and B, with citation

claim: Putative enhancers gaining H3K27me3 by P60 lose H3K27ac activity (termed 'Decommissioned').
source: These peak clusters were inversely associated with changes in H3K27ac levels over developmental time, such that putative enhancers gaining H3K27me3 by P60 lost activity (we term these 'Decommissioned')
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between H3K27me3 and H3K27ac at enhancers

claim: Putative enhancers losing H3K27me3 by P60 gain H3K27ac activity (termed 'Poised').
source: and putative enhancers losing H3K27me3 by P60 gained activity (we term these 'Poised').
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between H3K27me3 and H3K27ac at enhancers

claim: Four putative enhancers near Mycn were identified in the 'Decommissioned' cluster.
source: Within the 'Decommissioned' cluster, we identified 4 putative enhancers near Mycn that were also identified in the 'Developing Mouse Cerebellum Enhancer Atlas' (Ramirez et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by identification of enhancers and citation to Ramirez et al., 2022

claim: An enhancer near Grin2c was identified in the 'Poised' cluster that regulates Grin2c expression.
source: Within the 'Poised' cluster, we identified an enhancer near Grin2c in a region we previously showed regulates Grin2c expression (Frank et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by identification of the enhancer and citation to previous work

claim: Putative enhancers near Mycn and Grin2c physically interact with their promoters as measured by H3K4me3 PLAC-seq.
source: Both of these putative enhancers physically interact with the promoters of their putative target genes as measured by H3K4me3 PLAC-seq (Goodman et al., 2020) consistent with them playing a functional role in transcription.
evidence: The claim is supported by PLAC-seq data and citation to Goodman et al., 2020

claim: The majority (approximately 95%) of differential H3K27me3 peaks in developing mouse cerebellum do not overlap enhancers with H3K4me1.
source: These data show that although the vast majority (3411/3618; ~95%) of differential H3K27me3 peaks in developing mouse cerebellum do not overlap enhancers with H3K4me1
evidence: The claim is supported by calculation from overlap analysis

claim: Regulated changes in H3K27me3 are functionally important at a subset of enhancers for controlling developmentally regulated gene expression.
source: regulated changes in H3K27me3 are likely to be functionally important at a subset of these enhancers for controlling the expression of developmentally regulated genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between H3K27me3 changes and enhancer activity

claim: 13,409 differential H3K27ac peaks that are not at promoters were identified.
source: We identified 13,409 differential H3K27ac peaks that were not at promoters (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of H3K27ac ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: Only 214 (about 1.6%) of differential H3K27ac peaks also show developmentally regulated changes in H3K27me3.
source: However, only 214 of these, about 1.6%, also showed developmentally regulated changes in H3K27me3.
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis between differential H3K27ac and H3K27me3 peaks

claim: Developmental changes in H3K27me3 at CGN regulatory elements are biased toward gene promoters.
source: Thus although enhancers are crucially important regulatory elements for controlling cell type- and developmental stage-specific regulation of gene transcription (Nord and West, 2020), the developmental changes in H3K27me3 at CGN regulatory elements appears to be biased toward gene promoters.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low percentage of enhancers with differential H3K27me3 and citation

claim: RNA-seq counts show a developmental switch between dominant H3K27 methyltransferases and demethylases, but overall expression of each class does not substantially change over time.
source: At the level of gene expression, RNA-seq counts of the H3K27 methyltransferases Ezh1/2 and the H3K27 demethylases Kdm6a/b showed that although there was a developmental switch between the dominant reader and writer enzymes, the overall expression of each class of enzyme did not substantially change over time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Kdm6b expression is transiently induced in newborn CGNs in the inner EGL.
source: However, previous in situs from our lab demonstrated that Kdm6b expression is transiently induced in newborn CGNs in the inner EGL
evidence: The claim is supported by previous in situ hybridization data from the authors' lab

claim: shRNA-mediated knockdown of Kdm6b in cultured CGNs impairs the expression of a subset of developmentally induced genes.
source: and we further showed that shRNA-mediated knockdown of Kdm6b in cultured CGNs impairs the expression of a subset of developmentally induced genes (Wijayatunge et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by previous experimental data and citation to Wijayatunge et al., 2018

claim: KDM6B mediates the postmitotic loss of H3K27me3 at a subset of developmentally induced genes in the developing cerebellum in vivo.
source: Thus, we considered the possibility that KDM6B might mediate the postmitotic loss of H3K27me3 at a subset of developmentally induced genes in the developing cerebellum in vivo to promote their transcriptional induction.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on previous observations

claim: Conditional knockout of Kdm6b in cerebellar GNPs was achieved by crossing Atoh1-Cre mice with Kdm6bfl/fl mice.
source: To test this hypothesis, we conditionally knocked out Kdm6b in cerebellar GNPs in vivo by crossing heterozygous transgenic Atoh1-Cre mice with Kdm6bfl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach used

claim: 111 genes show significantly elevated expression in the Kdm6b-cKO at P14.
source: We found 111 genes that had significantly elevated expression in the Kdm6b-cKO
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis

claim: 150 genes show significantly reduced expression in the Kdm6b-cKO at P14.
source: and 150 that showed significantly reduced expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A

claim: Genes elevated at P14 in Kdm6b-cKO mice show developmentally regulated expression that is highest at P7 and falls by P60 in control mice.
source: Genes that were elevated at P14 in the Kdm6b-cKO mice all showed developmentally regulated expression in control mice that were highest at P7 and fell by P60.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of RNA-seq data between Kdm6b-cKO and control mice across developmental time

claim: Genes with reduced expression in Kdm6b-cKO mice show developmentally regulated expression that increases over developmental time in control mice.
source: Genes whose expression was reduced in the Kdm6b-cKO mice also showed developmentally regulated expression, but they increased in expression over developmental time.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of RNA-seq data between Kdm6b-cKO and control mice across developmental time

claim: Deletion of Kdm6b in GNPs slows the transcriptional maturation of CGNs in postnatal life.
source: Thus, the deletion of Kdm6b in GNPs appears to slow the transcriptional maturation of CGNs in postnatal life.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the gene expression changes observed in Kdm6b-cKO mice

claim: 250 H3K27me3 peaks are upregulated in Kdm6b-cKO compared to WT at P14.
source: We used DESeq2 to compute differentially enriched H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks between WT and Kdm6b-cKO tissue at P14, and obtained 250 upregulated peaks
evidence: The claim is supported by differential ChIP-seq peak analysis

claim: 327 H3K27me3 peaks are downregulated in Kdm6b-cKO compared to WT at P14.
source: and 327 downregulated peaks (FDR <0.05, |Log2FC|>1) (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by differential ChIP-seq peak analysis shown in Figure 4B

claim: Peaks with elevated H3K27me3 in Kdm6b-cKO mice are significantly more likely to be within gene promoters compared to the overall distribution of peaks.
source: We found peaks with elevated levels of H3K27me3 in Kdm6b-cKO mice to be significantly more likely to be within gene promoters compared with the overall distribution of peaks or the distribution of peaks that had reduced H3K27me3 in Kdm6b-cKO mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic annotation analysis of differential peaks

claim: Genes with promoters showing increased H3K27me3 in Kdm6b-cKO are enriched for neuronal GO terms.
source: The genes containing promoters with increased H3K27me3 in the Kdm6b-cKO were enriched for neuronal GO terms (Figure 4D)
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: Genes with promoters showing decreased H3K27me3 in Kdm6b-cKO mice failed to show significant GO terms.
source: whereas those containing promoters with decreased H3K27me3 in the Kdm6b-cKO mice failed to pull any significant GO terms.
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis

claim: Gain of H3K27me3 at promoters in Kdm6b-cKO is associated with significant loss of gene expression.
source: These data showed that the gain of H3K27me3 is associated with a significant loss of gene expression (Figure 4E)
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis between H3K27me3 ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4E

claim: Grin2c and Grm4 show increased H3K27me3 at their promoters and reduced expression in Kdm6b-cKO mice.
source: as exemplified by the synaptic glutamate receptor subunit genes Grin2c and Grm4 (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq tracks shown in Figure 4F

claim: Genes that lost H3K27me3 at their promoters in Kdm6b-cKO mice show no significant difference in gene expression.
source: By contrast, genes that lost H3K27me3 at their promoters in Kdm6b-cKO mice showed no significant difference in gene expression (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: Developmental loss of H3K27me3 at promoters of genes induced in maturing CGNs is facilitated by KDM6B.
source: These data suggest that developmental loss of H3K27me3 at the promoters of genes induced in CGNs during postmitotic maturation is facilitated by KDM6B
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Kdm6b-cKO experimental results

claim: H3K27me3 removal by KDM6B promotes the developmental induction of gene expression.
source: and that this H3K27me3 removal promotes the developmental induction of gene expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between H3K27me3 levels and gene expression in Kdm6b-cKO

claim: BART analysis predicts enrichment of PRC2 components EZH2, JARID2, and SUZ12 at both H3K27me3-Down promoters and all H3K27me3-promoter-associated genes.
source: As expected, we found PRC2 components EZH2, JARID2, and SUZ12 to be significantly enriched across both the H3K27me3-Down cluster and all H3K27me3-promoter-associated genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis of transcription factor binding

claim: Only the H3K27me3-Down cluster is significantly enriched for putative binding of transcription factors ZIC1 and ZIC2.
source: However, we found only the H3K27me3-Down cluster to be significantly enriched for the putative binding of transcription factors ZIC1 and ZIC2
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis

claim: ZIC1 and ZIC2 are drivers of CGN maturation.
source: which previous work from our group has shown to be a driver of CGN maturation (Frank et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work from the authors' group

claim: Both 'H3K27me3-Down (Fast)' and 'H3K27me3-Down (Slow)' clusters are enriched for ZIC1 and ZIC2 binding.
source: Importantly, when we assessed the 'H3K27me3-Down (Fast),' and 'H3K27me3-Down (Slow)' clusters separately (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), they were also enriched for the binding of ZIC1 and ZIC2
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A

claim: ZIC1 and ZIC2 function at multiple stages of CGN differentiation.
source: which is consistent with evidence (Frank et al., 2015) that these TFs function at multiple stages of CGN differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the enrichment in both Fast and Slow clusters and citation

claim: The 'H3K27me3-Up' cluster is significantly enriched for binding of SOX3, FOXF1, SHOX2, POU3F2, and HDAC1.
source: By contrast, when we performed the same analysis for the 'H3K27me3-Up' cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), we found this set of promoters was significantly enriched for the binding of a distinct set of TFs involved in cell differentiation, namely SOX3, FOXF1, SHOX2, POU3F2 as well as histone deacetylation (HDAC1) (Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citation

claim: ZIC1/2 enrichment increases most notably at genes with H3K27me3 Down compared to All Genes and Genes with H3K27me3 Up.
source: We found ZIC1/2 enrichment to increase most notably at Genes with H3K27me3 Down, compared to All Genes and Genes with H3K27me3 Up.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ZIC1/2 ChIP-seq data at different gene sets

claim: 56% of H3K27me3-Down genes are also ZIC-Up genes.
source: We found that 56% of H3K27me3-Down genes were also ZIC-Up
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis between H3K27me3-Down and ZIC-Up genes

claim: H3K27me3-Down genes that are also ZIC-Up are strongly enriched for neuronal GO terms.
source: and that these genes were strongly enriched for neuronal GO terms (Figure 5B)
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 5B

claim: 44% of H3K27me3-Down genes are not ZIC-Up and are enriched for generic cell-fate specification GO terms.
source: while the 44% of genes that were not ZIC-Up were enriched for generic cell-fate specification GO terms.
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis

claim: Only about 11% of H3K27me3-Up genes overlap with ZIC-Up genes.
source: As a control, we compared 'ZIC Up' genes to H3K27me3-Up genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and only found an overlap of only about 11%.
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A

claim: Gene promoters with H3K27me3 peaks 'Up in Kdm6b-cKO' show enrichment of putative ZIC1 and ZIC2 binding.
source: We repeated this analysis with the H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks that were differential at P14 between WT and Kdm6b-cKO described in Figure 4 and found a similar enrichment of putative ZIC1 and ZIC2 binding within gene promoters associated with H3K27me3 peaks 'Up in Kdm6b-cKO' (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: Gene promoters with H3K27me3 peaks 'Down in Kdm6b-cKO' do not show enrichment of putative ZIC1 and ZIC2 binding.
source: but not 'Down in Kdm6b-cKO' (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by BART analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: 72% of 'H3K27me3 Up in Kdm6b-cKO' genes are also 'ZIC Up' and are strongly enriched for neuronal GO terms.
source: 72% of the 'H3K27me3 Up in Kdm6b-cKO' genes were also 'ZIC Up' (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) and were strongly enriched for neuronal GO terms.
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap and Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: Only 9% of 'H3K27me3 Down in Kdm6b-cKO' genes are also 'ZIC Up'.
source: Only 9% of 'H3K27me3 Down in Kdm6b-cKO' were also 'ZIC Up' (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: Grin2c and Grm4 promoters are strongly enriched for ZIC1/2 at P60.
source: As examples of gene promoters that belong to both the H3K27me3-Down cluster, and H3K27me3 Up peaks due to Kdm6b-cKO, we show tracks for Grin2c and Grm4, which are strongly enriched for ZIC1/2 at their promoters at P60 (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ZIC ChIP-seq tracks shown in Figure 5C

claim: There is high concordance of gene expression changes between cerebellar maturation in vivo and in culture at early time points.
source: We found a high degree of concordance among genes expressed in vivo and in culture at early time points
evidence: The claim is supported by rank-rank hypergeometric overlap (RRHO) analysis

claim: There is weaker concordance of gene expression between in vivo and in culture at late time points, consistent with 7DIV representing a relatively early stage of in vivo development.

claim: The interaction between KDM6B and BAF complex plays a role in neuronal development.
source: This interaction has been shown to play a role in neuronal development (Narayanan et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Narayanan et al., 2015 and Nguyen et al., 2018

claim: Maturation of CGN transcriptional programs depends on the loss of H3K27me3 at genes that turn on late.
source: Interestingly, we find that maturation of CGN transcriptional programs not only depends on the loss of H3K27me3 at genes that turn on late
evidence: The claim is supported by the Kdm6b-cKO and GSK-126 experimental results

claim: Maturation of CGN transcriptional programs requires the addition of H3K27me3 at regions that gain this mark in newly postmitotic neurons.
source: but also requires the addition of H3K27me3 at regions that gain this mark in newly postmitotic neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the GSK-126 experimental results

claim: Rapid increases in H3K27me3 that accumulate in newly postmitotic neurons are highly sensitive to inhibition of EZH2 with GSK-126.
source: Using CUT&RUN in cultured CGNs, we discovered that the rapid increases in H3K27me3 that accumulate in newly postmitotic neurons are highly sensitive to inhibition of EZH2 with GSK-126.
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&RUN analysis after GSK-126 treatment

claim: Failure to gain H3K27me3 at specific sites in differentiating neurons prevents developmental downregulation of CGN progenitor markers like Mycn, Jag1, and Ebf3.
source: Failure to gain H3K27me3 at these sites in differentiating neurons not only prevented the developmental downregulation of CGN progenitor markers like Mycn, Jag1, and Ebf3
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis after GSK-126 treatment

claim: Failure to gain H3K27me3 at specific sites in differentiating neurons impairs developmental induction of late genes like Gabrd, Grm4, and Grin2c.
source: but also impaired the developmental induction of late genes like Gabrd, Grm4, and Grin2c.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis after GSK-126 treatment

claim: The impact of GSK-126 on the mature CGN transcriptional program is not due to changes in H3K27me3 regulation at promoters of the late genes themselves.
source: The impact of GSK-126 on the mature CGN transcriptional program, however, was not due to changes in H3K27me3 regulation at promoters of the late genes themselves.
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&RUN analysis showing no change in H3K27me3 at late gene promoters after GSK-126 treatment

claim: The postmitotic addition of H3K27me3 at specific genomic sites is crucial in regulating the induction of genes that turn on well after neuronal cell fate is determined.
source: This shows that the postmitotic addition of H3K27me3 at specific genomic sites is crucial in regulating the induction of genes that turn on well after neuronal cell fate is determined.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the GSK-126 experimental results

claim: Knocking out EZH2 in postmitotic neuronal cultures results in loss of H3K27me3 at the Prdm13 promoter and enhanced expression of this transcriptional repressor, which then leads indirectly to reduced expression of its target genes.
source: One prior study that reported the consequences of knocking out EZH2 in postmitotic neuronal cultures showed that this resulted in the loss of H3K27me3 at the promoter of the Prdm13 gene and enhanced expression of this transcriptional repressor, which they suggested then led indirectly to reduced expression of its target genes in the knockout neurons (Buontempo et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Buontempo et al., 2022

claim: Prdm13 expression and promoter H3K27me3 are unaffected by EZH2 inhibition in DIV5 CGNs.
source: Though a similar mechanism could be at play in our cultures, Prdm13 expression and promoter H3K27me3 were unaffected by EZH2 inhibition in our DIV5 CGNs
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of Prdm13 in the GSK-126 treated CGNs

claim: Developmental gains in H3K27me3 during postmitotic differentiation are relatively equally split between promoters, gene bodies, and distal intergenic regions.
source: Notably, developmental gains in H3K27me3 during postmitotic differentiation are relatively equally split between promoters, gene bodies, and distal intergenic regions (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic annotation analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: The majority of non-promoter peaks of H3K27me3 do not overlap enhancers.
source: By comparing these sites of H3K27me3 regulation to other chromatin marks, we found that the majority of non-promoter peaks of H3K27me3 do not overlap enhancers.
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis with enhancer marks

claim: H3K27me3 might contribute to gene regulation through an alternate mechanism such as by impacting chromatin architecture.
source: These data raise the possibility that rather than functioning to control transcriptional regulatory elements directly, H3K27me3 might contribute to gene regulation through an alternate mechanisms such as by impacting chromatin architecture.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing an alternative mechanism

claim: PRC2-dependent deposition of H3K27me3 has been shown to contribute to physical interactions between enhancers and their target genes by anchoring chromatin loops.
source: PRC2-dependent deposition of H3K27me3 has been shown in some cases to contribute to physical interactions between enhancers and their target genes by anchoring chromatin loops (Cruz-Molina et al., 2017; Kraft et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cruz-Molina et al., 2017 and Kraft et al., 2022

claim: Chromatin loops anchored by H3K27me3 may poise genes for enhancer activation later upon receiving a developmental stimulus.
source: These loops may then poise genes for enhancer activation later upon receiving a developmental stimulus.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from cited studies

claim: The gain of H3K27me3 in early differentiating CGNs could establish enhancer contacts with promoters of late genes such that when KDM6B demethylates these promoters, the enhancer can permit activation.
source: The gain of H3K27me3 in early differentiating CGNs could serve a similar function to establish such enhancer contacts with the promoters of late genes such that when KDM6B demethylates these promoters, the enhancer can permit activation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a mechanism for how H3K27me3 gain and loss coordinate gene activation

claim: Investigating dynamics in higher-order chromatin structure through techniques like HiCAR might help inform how H3K27me3 dynamics contribute to gene regulation in postmitotic neurons.
source: In the future, investigating dynamics in higher-order chromatin structure through low-input techniques such as HiCAR (Wei et al., 2022) might help inform how H3K27me3 dynamics contribute to gene regulation in postmitotic neurons.
evidence: The claim is a recommendation for future research with citation
